message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus reasonable deductions for damage beyond normal wear. | • Keep records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | • Report problems promptly; landlords must respond within a reasonable time. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may pay the repair cost and deduct from rent, or withhold rent until repairs are made. | • Document all repair requests and responses. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (except emergencies). | • Landlords must give 24‑hour written notice before entry. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements. | • Written notices are required; keep copies. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • Fair Housing Act applies; file complaints if discrimination occurs. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for month‑to‑month agreements.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions. | • Review lease carefully; negotiate terms. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must comply with any local ordinances. | • Check city ordinances (e.g., Austin, Houston) for rent‑control rules. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper legal process: serve a notice, file a complaint, attend court. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court; they have the right to a hearing. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect tenant privacy; cannot conduct searches without consent or a warrant. | • Know your rights regarding landlord access. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities unless otherwise agreed. | • Verify utility responsibilities in lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Landlord may require written permission; cannot unreasonably deny. | • Obtain written approval before subletting. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to insure the unit; tenants may obtain renter’s insurance. | • Consider renter’s insurance for personal property protection. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep written records of all communications, receipts, and photographs of the unit’s condition. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with Texas Property Code § 24.001–24.999 and local ordinances. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipts to establish proof. 4. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face disputes, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local tenant‑advocacy organization. 5. **File Complaints** – If you suspect unlawful behavior, file complaints with the Texas Attorney General’s Office or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Tenant Rights**: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection/tenant-rights - **Texas Property Code**: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PC/htm/PC.24.htm - **Local Tenant‑Advocacy Groups** – e.g., Austin Tenants Union, Houston Tenant Coalition. If you need a specific legal document (e.g., a lease agreement or a notice of rent increase), let me know and I can help generate it.
